summary: Focused validation of NEW auth features (email verification, forgot/reset password, refresh-token rotation, logout, silent-refresh UI). Added 13 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/test_auth_new.py — ALL 13 PASS. Verified all 4 new UI pages via Playwright (Login has forgot-password-link, /forgot-password shows sent-confirmation, /reset-password shows invalid-token when token missing and mismatch error when passwords differ, /verify-email shows verify-error for invalid/missing token). Verified silent-refresh interceptor end-to-end in the browser: corrupted access token is transparently refreshed via /auth/refresh, refreshToken is rotated in localStorage, protected page load succeeds without redirect to /login. Regression suite from iteration_1 re-run: 25/26 pass (1 flaky COD-order test — passed on retry, unrelated to auth changes).

minor.issue: Flaky — one full-suite run returned 404 'Record not found', but the same test passed in isolation and via curl immediately after. Suspect Prisma transaction / inventory decrement race when the same product is used in Razorpay create-order + COD create-order back to back. Not caused by the new auth work.
Still returns full stack traces in prod-facing responses (NODE_ENV=development). Same finding as iteration_1 — not fixed.

action_items: Investigate flaky COD order 404 (not caused by auth work, but worth a look — probably around orderController stock decrement / coupon record lookup when a Razorpay order was just created).
critical_code_review_comments: authRoutes.js exposes BOTH POST and GET /verify-email — GET has no CSRF risk here (token is single-use) but keep in mind email clients often GET the link; ensure the GET handler returns something browser-friendly (currently it calls the same controller which likely returns JSON — from user perspective they hit the /verify-email FE route with ?token, which posts to the API, so this is fine).

client/src/services/api.js: silent-refresh implementation is solid — single-flight guard (isRefreshing + refreshWaiters), skips /auth/refresh|login|register|forgot|reset from being retried, rotates refreshToken in localStorage. One minor gotcha: if the app cold-boots on a protected page with a stale access token and NO refreshToken, the interceptor still redirects to /login (good).

ForgotPassword.jsx sets sent=true even when the API errors (see try/catch — sent is set BEFORE toast.success and NOT reset in catch). Actually it IS inside try before await resolves — good. But if the API returns non-2xx (network), it will jump to catch and setSent(true) will NOT run — correct behaviour. No issue.
ResetPassword.jsx validates password length client-side (min 8) but does not surface backend Zod validation errors distinctly — currently shows the generic 'Reset failed' toast. Acceptable.
VerifyEmail.jsx uses a useRef(ran) guard so React 18 StrictMode double-invocation doesn't consume the token twice — good defensive coding.
Backend log leaks the reset/verification link in cleartext — intended for TEST/dev; make sure NODE_ENV=production suppresses these console.log lines in email.js.

success_rate.backend: 100% (13/13 new auth + 25/26 regression; 1 flaky COD not related)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (all requested testids present and behave as specified; silent-refresh verified in real browser)

context_for_next_testing_agent: 1) To fetch fresh verify/reset tokens during a test, tail /var/log/supervisor/ecom_server.out.log for lines starting with '[email] Verification link' or '[email] Password reset link' — token is the ?token=... query param. 2) When running the existing pytest suite, use `-n 0` (serial) — the tests share state via pytest module attributes (pytest.first_id, pytest.reg_token) which xdist would split across workers and break. 3) The response envelope {status:'success',data:{...}} is unwrapped on the frontend by the axios interceptor; tests should handle BOTH shapes via `d = r.json().get('data') or r.json()`. 4) Silent refresh was validated by corrupting `state.token` in localStorage while keeping `state.refreshToken` intact, then navigating to /profile — the interceptor caught the 401, called /auth/refresh, rotated both tokens, and re-issued the original request. 5) All new UI pages honor the exact data-testids from the request (forgot-password-page, forgot-sent-message, forgot-email, forgot-submit, reset-password-page, reset-invalid-token, reset-password, reset-confirm, reset-submit, verify-email-page, verify-success, verify-error, forgot-password-link).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no blocking bugs found. Every new auth feature listed in the review request works as designed and backward compatibility is preserved (login still stores token in localStorage 'auth-storage' and now ALSO stores refreshToken alongside).
